tools.name: daytona_api_create_sandbox
tools.title: Create a new sandbox
tools.description: Create a new sandbox

name.description: The name of the sandbox. If not provided, the sandbox ID will be used as the name

snapshot.description: The ID or name of the snapshot used for the sandbox

user.description: The user associated with the project

public.description: Whether the sandbox http preview is publicly accessible

networkBlockAll.description: Whether to block all network access for the sandbox

kvm.description: Expose KVM (/dev/kvm) inside the sandbox via nested virtualization. linux-vm snapshots only. Requires the sandbox_kvm feature for the organization.

networkAllowList.description: Comma-separated list of allowed CIDR network addresses for the sandbox

domainAllowList.description: Comma-separated list of allowed domains for the sandbox

outboundProxyUrl.description: Outbound proxy URL to route the sandbox HTTP(S) traffic through (http or https; credentials may be included in the URL). On its own this is convenience routing, not a security boundary: it is applied by injecting the standard HTTP(S)_PROXY environment variables at creation, so a process that clears those variables egresses directly. Combine with domainAllowList to have web-port (80/443) egress transparently redirected through the proxy chain at the network layer, which cannot be bypassed from inside the sandbox.

otelEndpointOverride.description: OTel collector endpoint override for this sandbox. When set, sandbox OTel data is sent to this endpoint instead of the default collector (the Daytona-hosted collector or the region-configured endpoint) and will not be available in the Daytona analytics API or dashboard.

target.description: The target (region) where the sandbox will be created

cpu.description: CPU cores allocated to the sandbox

gpu.description: GPU units allocated to the sandbox

gpuType.description: Preferred GPU type for the sandbox. Accepts a single value or an ordered preference list — the scheduler tries each in order and pins the sandbox to the first that has capacity.

spot.description: GPU-only. When true, the sandbox may be instantly terminated without notice to free GPU capacity for an on-demand (non-spot) GPU sandbox. Ignored / rejected when the sandbox requests no GPUs.

memory.description: Memory allocated to the sandbox in GB

disk.description: Disk space allocated to the sandbox in GB

autoStopInterval.description: Auto-stop interval in minutes (0 means disabled)

autoPauseInterval.description: Auto-pause interval in minutes (0 means disabled). Only supported for sandbox classes that support pausing. Not allowed for ephemeral sandboxes. At most one of autoStopInterval and autoPauseInterval may be non-zero. For non-ephemeral sandbox classes that support pausing, defaults to 60 minutes (with auto-stop disabled) when neither interval is provided.

autoArchiveInterval.description: Auto-archive interval in minutes (0 means the maximum interval will be used)

autoDeleteInterval.description: Auto-delete interval in minutes (negative value means disabled, 0 means delete immediately upon stopping)

ttlMinutes.description: Maximum time to live in minutes, counted as wall-clock time since creation regardless of sandbox state (0 means disabled). When it elapses the sandbox is destroyed, even if it is stopped, paused, or archived. Subject to the maximum sandbox lifespan configured for the organization region and sandbox class, in which case it also defaults to that maximum and cannot be disabled.

queueTimeout.description: Minutes to wait for runner assignment before cancelling sandbox creation. Applies only while the sandbox is unassigned in pending_build or pulling_snapshot. Only honored when default queue timeout is enabled for the organization. Omit to use the organization default; null/omit with no organization default leaves the wait unlimited. Must be a positive integer.

volumes.description: Array of volumes to attach to the sandbox

linkedSandbox.description: ID or name of an existing sandbox to link the new sandbox to. The new sandbox will be scheduled on the same runner as the linked sandbox so a local network can be established between them. Linked sandboxes must be ephemeral (autoDeleteInterval=0) and cannot themselves be linked to another sandbox. GPU sandboxes cannot participate in links in either direction: a GPU sandbox cannot specify linkedSandbox, and cannot be the link target of another sandbox.

secrets.description: Secrets to mount in this sandbox. Each entry maps an env var name to a vault secret name.

volumeId.description: The ID or name of the volume. Resolved to the volume ID on sandbox create.

mountPath.description: The mount path for the volume

subpath.description: Optional subpath within the volume to mount. When specified, only this S3 prefix will be accessible. When omitted, the entire volume is mounted.

dockerfileContent.description: The Dockerfile content used for the build

contextHashes.description: The context hashes used for the build

tools.description: Execute Python, JavaScript, or TypeScript code and return output, exit code, and artifacts

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_execute_command
tools.title: Execute a command
tools.description: Execute a shell command and return the output and exit code

envs.description: Environment variables to set for the command

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds, defaults to 10 seconds

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_list_interpreter_contexts
tools.title: List all user-created interpreter contexts
tools.description: Returns information about all user-created interpreter contexts (excludes default context)

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_create_interpreter_context
tools.title: Create a new interpreter context
tools.description: Creates a new isolated interpreter context with optional working directory and language

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_delete_interpreter_context
tools.title: Delete an interpreter context
tools.description: Deletes an interpreter context and shuts down its worker process

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_list_pty_sessions
tools.title: List all PTY sessions
tools.description: Get a list of all active pseudo-terminal sessions

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_create_pty_session
tools.title: Create a new PTY session
tools.description: Create a new pseudo-terminal session with specified configuration

lazyStart.description: Don't start PTY until first client connects

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_delete_pty_session
tools.title: Delete a PTY session
tools.description: Delete a pseudo-terminal session and terminate its process

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_get_pty_session
tools.title: Get PTY session information
tools.description: Get detailed information about a specific pseudo-terminal session

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_resize_pty_session
tools.title: Resize a PTY session
tools.description: Resize the terminal dimensions of a pseudo-terminal session

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_list_sessions
tools.title: List all sessions
tools.description: Get a list of all active shell sessions

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_create_session
tools.title: Create a new session
tools.description: Create a new shell session for command execution

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_get_entrypoint_session
tools.title: Get entrypoint session details
tools.description: Get details of an entrypoint session including its commands

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_get_entrypoint_logs
tools.title: Get entrypoint logs
tools.description: Get logs for a sandbox entrypoint session. Returns JSON with separated stdout/stderr for SDK >= 0.161.0, plain text otherwise. Supports WebSocket streaming.

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_delete_session
tools.title: Delete a session
tools.description: Delete an existing shell session

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_get_session
tools.title: Get session details
tools.description: Get details of a specific session including its commands

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_get_session_command
tools.title: Get session command details
tools.description: Get details of a specific command within a session

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_send_input
tools.title: Send input to command
tools.description: Send input data to a running command in a session for interactive execution

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_get_session_command_logs
tools.title: Get session command logs
tools.description: Get logs for a specific command within a session. Returns JSON with separated stdout/stderr for SDK >= 0.167.0, plain text otherwise. Supports WebSocket streaming.

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_session_execute_command
tools.title: Execute command in session
tools.description: Execute a command within an existing shell session

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_get_system_metrics
tools.title: Get sandbox resource metrics
tools.description:
Latest CPU/memory/disk usage snapshot for the sandbox. cpuUsedPct is the
average CPU usage as a percentage of the CPU limit over the last sample
window (0 until the first sample completes). Byte fields are in bytes.

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_get_user_home_dir
tools.title: Get user home directory
tools.description: Get the current user home directory path.

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_get_version
tools.title: Get version
tools.description: Get the current daemon version

tools.name: daytona_toolbox_get_work_dir
tools.title: Get working directory
tools.description: Get the current working directory path. This is default directory used for running commands.
